title: Flowise prediction API -- T1565.001 overrideConfig spreads unchecked into flow execution context, enabling session hijack and chat-history injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69258 (GHSA-6vh2-wg4h-4vwj),
affecting the unauthenticated (whitelisted) `POST /api/v1/prediction/:id`
endpoint.

A prior advisory (GHSA-5cph-wvm9-45gj) gated `overrideConfig`'s
ability to modify node input parameters behind `apiOverrideStatus`.
Two SEPARATE spread operations were not covered by that fix:
`buildChatflow.ts` spreads `incomingInput.overrideConfig` directly
into `flowConfig`, and `utils/index.ts` does the same into
`flowData` -- both unconditionally, with no `apiOverrideStatus`
check, even though the sibling node-parameter path correctly checks
it. `flowConfig` feeds the `$flow.*` template variable resolver, so
any attacker-injected property becomes available to any node
template referencing it. Concretely: `overrideConfig: {"chatId":
"<victim-id>"}` on an unauthenticated request redirects the
attacker's messages and responses into the victim's conversation
memory session; `overrideConfig: {"chatHistory": [...]}` injects a
fabricated system message as prompt injection with no UI interaction
at all.

Detection logic flags a `POST /api/v1/prediction/:id` request whose
`overrideConfig` object sets `chatId`, `sessionId`, or `chatHistory`
-- the exact ungated properties this advisory's proof of concept
demonstrates flow, unauthenticated, straight into the execution
context that controls which conversation session is read and
written.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact two ungated spread locations, contrasting them
against the correctly-gated sibling code path, and three concrete
attack scenarios each with a working curl reproduction), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
